# 209 — PR explainer (full walkthrough + quiz; written to satisfy the HIGH-tier deliverable regardless of the tier the verifier assigns — see `209.md` §Risk tier, size-cap caveat)

## Goal

Four assertions across three of the audit's own guard tests were **red on `main`**. This item turns them
green **by re-pointing them at what the product actually does today** — without relaxing a single one, and
without touching one line of product code.

## The intuition, in one paragraph

Normally a red test on `main` means the product broke. These four mean the opposite: **the product got
better and the guards went red for it.** Three shipped items widened something —

- **203** started appending `&src=seo_token` to every estate pool link (the north-star attribution rail),
- **199** started emitting `lensPick` surfaces (@360px / @dark / @ko) alongside rotation picks,
- **201** widened the bloom responsive check from 360-only to 360 **and** 768 —

and each widening's own test went green while three older tests, which pinned the *old* literal (an exact
URL shape, an exact array length, the string `s.width <= 360`), started failing. Nobody had classified
them; the 206 verifier found them on a clean `origin/main` worktree and filed them for a future item.
This is that item.

## Why it was worth a build slot

`package.json`'s `test:serial` is **the only pre-ship gate this repo has** (item 205: there is no test CI —
`.github/workflows/` holds `sitemap-update.yml` alone). All four failing assertions are `fixture wiring
check`s — **preconditions guarding a guard**: they exist to prove the pool-link-liveness gate, the
rotation-honesty accounting, and the bloom detector set are pointed at something real. Two of the three
files guard machinery on the **north-star `?pool=` surface**, and one guards the rotation accounting item
**206 shipped the day before** onto the widened 3,984-candidate arrival population.

before and after.

## The part that actually matters: non-vacuity

Making a red assertion green is trivial and usually wrong. Each repair therefore ships with a proof that
it **still goes red for the reason it exists**, produced by mutating the *input* on a scratch copy — never
the assertion, never a committed file (full transcripts in `209-notes.md`):

- regex — an anchor whose `?pool=` shape is genuinely absent still trips the check (and the same regex
  still matches the real page today, so the proof isn't vacuous in the other direction);
- partition — a wrong rotation-pick count still fails, **and** a surface carrying neither `rotationPick`
  nor `lensPick` still fails;
- bloom — a branch with **no** `checkResponsive` call fails, **and** one with an *unscoped* (all-viewport)
  call fails. Both directions, because a one-directional proof is how a vacuous green ships.

## Results

`test_audit_pool_link_liveness.js` 11/1 → **12/0** · `test_audit_cta_provenance.js` 33/2 → **35/0** ·
`test_audit_planner_flow.js` 10/1 → **11/0**. No `test()` block added or removed — the counts rise because
the previously-failing assertions now pass. `npm run test:fast` → **42 pass / 0 fail / 0 timeout**. The
88-file browser lane was **not** run and is **not** claimed green (5-minute foreground timebox, standing
decision 2026-07-11).

## Deliberately not done

- `test_seo_surface_audit.js` — the **5th** pre-existing red. Item 185 owns it (rule F, stale proxy
  metric); it also exceeds the timebox. Reported, not absorbed, not fixed. *One item, one red class.*
- No product file touched. If a repair had appeared to need one, the classification would have been wrong
  and the right move would have been to stop, not to edit `audit-app.js`.

## Compound step

`playbooks/pre-existing-red-triage.md` gains **decision rule H** — the rule-B *widening* variant, the class
none of A–G had a slot for: observed is a **superset** of expected (not a contradiction), the failing
assertion is a **precondition** while the behavioural ones stay green, and the widening's own test is green
with the owning item named in a product-code comment. Resolution H is the "re-point at the class, never at
the new literal" recipe (tolerate-and-preserve · partition-then-classify-the-remainder · re-derive every
downstream use, including the green ones), plus the one-line prevention: **`grep -rn '<the old literal>'
test_*.js` before shipping any widening.** All three of this item's reds would have cost their authors one
line each.

## Quiz (HIGH-tier deliverable, written regardless of the tier the verifier assigns)

1. Three of these four reds were caused by shipped items 199, 201 and 203. Does that mean any of those
   three items introduced a product bug? Justify from the diff.
2. The repair at both `test_audit_cta_provenance.js` sites adds an assertion the original never had:
   `nonRotationSurfaces.every(s => s.lensPick === true)`. Adding assertions to a red test is normally
   suspicious — why is this one the point of the item rather than scope creep?
3. In `test_audit_pool_link_liveness.js`, the id swap now re-inserts the captured query tail
   (`$1${fakeId}$3$4`). What specifically breaks about that test's *meaning* if the tail is dropped?
4. What would it take for the `s.width <= 768` repair to be a **vacuous** green, and which of the
   item's proofs rules that out?
5. A fifth pre-existing red exists and this item did not fix it. Name it, name its rule, and say why
   leaving it is the correct call rather than an omission.
